battle.name: 滿城之戰
battle.brief: 滿城之戰是宋遼戰爭的反擊之戰。979年九月，遼景宗乘高梁河之捷，遣韓匡嗣、耶律休哥率十萬眾自幽州南下，直指河北重鎮鎮州；宋軍以劉廷翰、李漢瓊、崔翰、崔彥進分統八萬人拒於徐河，趙廷進、李繼隆力主變陣。終場斬首萬餘級、俘老幼三萬戶，遼軍退易州；步戰仍賴長矛，本卡埃及長矛即其先例。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這是一場北宋與遼朝之間的邊境會戰，交戰地在河北易州—滿城—遂城一線的中路防線上。北宋方面，太平興國四年五月太宗親征滅北漢，六月移師圍幽州，七月高梁河一戰主力崩潰，軍心與國力都需要一段恢復期；但幽雲十六州仍握在契丹手中，宋廷不甘罷手，遂以關南、定州、鎮州三處重鎮為樞軸，部署沿線屯兵，一旦遼軍南下便互相策應。統兵序列以鎮州兵馬都監李繼隆、雲州觀察使兼鎮州駐泊都鈐轄劉廷翰、彰德軍節度使李漢瓊、殿前都虞侯端州團練使崔翰、河陽三城節度使崔彥進為主，另有西上閣門副使薛繼興、閣門祗候李守斌分屯關南；全軍依太宗所頒「平戎萬全陣圖」分為八陣，總兵力約八萬，由三鎮之師拼合而成，指揮體系是中樞節制、將校分領，遇敵則由前線將官自行決斷。遼朝方面，景宗耶律賢以燕京遭圍為由下詔南伐，遣燕王韓匡嗣為南面行軍都統，耶律沙為監軍，耶律休哥為副帥，耶律斜軫、耶律抹只各率一軍應徵，主力十萬自幽州出發，經易州南下，兵鋒直指滿城與遂城，圖取河北重鎮鎮州；另以耶律善補一部趨河東路，牽制宋軍側翼。遼軍以契丹騎兵為骨幹，輔以漢地降附之兵，聽命於燕王與北面諸將，是典型的騎兵統帥加多路分遣體系。
countriesEn: This was a frontier engagement between the Northern Song and the Liao (Khitan) dynasty, fought on the central sector of the Hebei defence line that ran from Yi Prefecture through Mancheng to Suicheng. On the Song side, Emperor Taizong personally campaigned to destroy the Northern Han in the fifth month of Taiping Xingguo 4 (979) and turned his army north in the sixth month to besiege Youzhou; the Song host was shattered at Gaolianghe in the seventh month, and both the fighting spirit of the troops and the resources of the treasury needed time to recover. The Sixteen Prefectures of Yun-Yan nevertheless remained in Khitan hands and the Song court would not let the matter drop, so garrison troops were posted along the axis of the three great towns of Guannan, Dingzhou and Zhenzhou, ready to cover one another the moment the Liao moved south. The command roster was headed by Li Jilong, military supervisor of Zhenzhou, Liu Tinghan, circuit intendant of Yunzhou and deputy commander of the Zhenzhou garrison, Li Hanqiong, military governor of Zhangde, Cui Han, palace commandant of the Northern Guard and military commissioner of Dingwu, and Cui Yanjin, military governor of Hedong Three Cities; Xue Jixing, deputy director of the Western Palace Attendants, and Li Shaobin, a palace attendant of the Guards, held Guannan. The whole army was broken into eight lines according to the Perfect Array for Pacifying the Rong issued by the emperor, numbering about eighty thousand men in all, assembled out of the three garrisons, under a command arrangement of central supervision with the field generals deciding in person. On the Liao side, Emperor Jingzong of Liao, Yelü Xian, issued the order to invade to avenge the siege of Yanjing, naming the Prince of Yan, Han Kuangsi, commander-in-chief of the southern campaign, Yelü Sha the supervisor and Yelü Xiuge the deputy, with Yelü Shezhen and Yelü Mozhi each leading a separate column. The main host of some one hundred thousand men left Youzhou, passed through Yi Prefecture and drove straight at Mancheng and Suicheng in an attempt to seize Zhenzhou, the great Song stronghold in Hebei; a further force under Yelü Shanbu was turned toward Hedong Circuit as a diversion. The Liao army was built on Khitan cavalry backed by troops from the Chinese-administered regions and answered to the Prince of Yan and the northern commanders, a typical cavalry command structure reinforced by multiple detached columns.
people: 宋軍一方最具決定性的人物不是太宗，而是前線幾位敢於變陣的將官。鎮州兵馬都監李繼隆在太宗頒下的「平戎萬全陣圖」被前方將校視為死板而無用時，說出「兵貴適變，安可預定」並主動請責，終於拍板改陣；右龍武將軍趙廷進（部分文獻作趙延進）登高觀陣，見遼軍「東西互野，不見其尾」，力主把星羅棋布的八陣合併為二陣、前後相輔，說「不如合而擊之，可以決勝」，又以「違令而失利，不猶勝於辱國乎」打消眾將顧慮，若敗願獨當其責；定武軍節度使崔翰起初擔心擅改詔命而不敢應允，待李繼隆擔保之後才下定決心。雲州觀察使劉廷翰是最先投入行動的人，得知遼軍南下即率眾北進二百里，搶在徐河灘頭列陣，並奪取河上的橋梁；河陽三城節度使崔彥進則潛師黑蘆堤北、緣長城口銜枚尾隨敵後，意在斷其歸路；李漢瓊與崔翰兩部隨後趕到會合，全軍才達八萬之眾。基層的指揮使丁罕在爭橋之戰中奪橋有功，戰後遷本軍都虞侯。遼方最高指揮是燕王韓匡嗣，此人雖掛南面行軍都統之名，卻在關鍵時刻輕信宋軍詐降、臨陣失措，最後棄旗鼓而走；副帥耶律休哥力主嚴兵以待卻未被採納。戰後遼主以違眾深入、行伍不整、棄師鼠竄、偵候失機、捐棄旗鼓五罪責韓匡嗣，幾欲加刑，幸得皇后力救才免於死，隨後改由耶律休哥總攝南面戍兵。
peopleEn: The decisive figures on the Song side were not the emperor but the field generals who dared to change the given order of battle. Li Jilong, military supervisor of Zhenzhou, when the Perfect Array for Pacifying the Rong issued by Taizong was dismissed by the commanders on the ground as rigid and useless, spoke the words arming the troops must adapt to circumstance, that no plan can be fixed in advance, and volunteered to bear the charge of disobedience; it was he who finally authorised the change. Zhao Tingjin (written Zhao Yanjin in some texts), Right Dragon and Martial General, climbed a vantage point to observe the Liao host, saw that the enemy deployed east and west in open country with no tail in sight, and argued that the eight lines scattered like stars should be merged into two mutually supporting lines front and rear, declaring that it was better to strike in force and win than to be humiliated by the nation, and offering to bear the sole responsibility should the plan fail. Cui Han, military governor of Dingwu, at first dared not consent for fear of altering the imperial decree, and only after Li Jilong's guarantee did he make up his mind. Liu Tinghan, circuit intendant of Yunzhou, was the first to move: as soon as he learned the Liao were marching south he led his men two hundred li north, deployed at the sandbank of the Xu River and seized the bridge over it. Cui Yanjin, military governor of Hedong Three Cities, took a detachment by stealth through the north of Black Reed Bank, along the Great Wall gap, moving with the soldiers holding their breath, to fall upon the enemy's rear and cut off its line of retreat. The troops of Li Hanqiong and Cui Han then closed up and joined them, bringing the Song force to its full strength of some eighty thousand. At the lower level, the company commander Ding Han earned promotion to deputy commandant of the army for his part in taking the bridge. The highest Liao command was held by the Prince of Yan, Han Kuangsi, who bore the title commander-in-chief of the southern campaign yet at the critical moment believed the Song offer of surrender, lost his composure and finally fled abandoning his flags and drums; the deputy, Yelü Xiuge, had urged him to tighten the ranks and wait, and was not heeded. Afterwards the Liao ruler charged Han Kuangsi with five counts of failure — advancing too deep against the general will, disorderly ranks, abandoning the army and fleeing like a rat, missing the opportunity in reconnaissance, and throwing away flags and drums — and ordered his execution; only the intercession of the empress saved him, and command of the southern garrisons passed to Yelü Xiuge.
kits: 卡面所繪的「埃及長矛」屬於早王朝時期埃及的守城冷兵器：銅或青銅矛頭纏固於木杆，形制承自新石器時代的標槍傳統，是「矛」這一類兵器在金屬時代最早的成熟樣式。它並非滿城之戰的出土物，也不曾出現在河北的戰場上，但正因為矛是古代世界最普及的近身兵器，這張卡面便以它的源流為代表，串起本戰役的裝備骨架。就同期而言，公元十世紀末的埃及正處於法蒂瑪王朝治下，其步兵骨幹裝備同樣不外乎矛、弓箭與短兵，只在金屬材質與裝飾上更見精華。九百年後的中原與契丹前線，矛的分量絲毫不減：宋軍步卒持長矛長槊列陣，槍首作柳葉形或菱形，槍身多長於一丈，配以皮盾或棗木盾，弓箭手配神臂弓一類強弩，另備拒馬與刺馬椿一類阻斷騎兵的器材；火器方面，宋軍在遼境戰役中已用上以火藥填充的火箭與「火砲」，但射程與精度仍遠不足以取代冷兵器。遼軍的裝備重心在騎兵與弓箭：契丹馬上冷兵器以馬槊、札刀、鐧刀為主，近身格鬥輔以骨朵一類打擊鈍器，步卒則用短矛與盾，弓弩數量龐大，騎兵多賴馬匹衝撞與繞射。韓匡嗣敗後棄旗鼓而走，說明旗鼓與號令器材在遼軍編制中同樣是樞紐，一旦主將的中軍失措，全軍便失去方向。此外，本役的工程性器材集中於徐河橋、拒馬與黑蘆堤一線的渡河、斷路與設伏，長城口與河灘地形直接決定了迂回部隊的可行性。冷兵器仍是這場戰爭真正決定勝負的物質基礎。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card face belongs to the defensive cold armament of Egypt in the Early Dynastic period: a copper or bronze head bound onto a wooden shaft, a form inherited from the Neolithic javelin tradition, and one of the earliest mature shapes taken by the spear class in the metal age. It is not an artefact from the battle of Mancheng and it never stood on a Hebei battlefield; but because the spear was the most widespread close-combat weapon in the ancient world, the card takes its lineage as a representative in order to frame the material backbone of this campaign. For the contemporary parallel, in the late tenth century Egypt was ruled by the Fatimid caliphate, whose infantry relied no less on spears, bows and short weapons, though their metalwork and decoration were far more refined. Nine centuries later, on the Central Plain and on the Khitan front line, the spear had lost nothing of its weight: Song infantry formed up with long spears and lang-jiang, the heads usually willow-leaf or lozenge shaped and the shafts often more than one zhang in length, supported by leather or jujube-wood shields, with powerful crossbows such as the divine-arm bow among the bowmen, plus cheval-de-frise and horse-choking stakes to check charging cavalry. As for firearms, Song troops in the fighting beyond the Liao border already used fire-arrows and the huo-pao charged with gunpowder, but their range and accuracy remained far short of replacing cold weapons. The Liao armament centred on cavalry and the bow: among the Khitan, the cold weapons used from the saddle were the ma-jue, zha-dao and chan-dao, with club-like striking weapons such as the bone club in close fighting, while infantry carried short spears and shields; bows and crossbows were numerous, and cavalry relied on the impact of the horse and on shooting from the saddle. Han Kuangsi's flight with his flags and drums abandoned showed that banners and signalling equipment were just as pivotal in the Liao order of battle, and that once a commander's centre lost its nerve the whole army lost its direction. The engineering materials of this engagement cluster around the Xu River bridge, the cheval-de-frise line and the Black Reed Bank, where fords, road-cutting and ambushes were the order of the day, and the terrain of the Great Wall gap and the river sandbanks decided outright whether the flanking column could operate. Cold weapons remained the material foundation on which the outcome of this war was truly decided.
tactics: 遼軍採聲東擊西、大縱深直取的戰法：主力十萬自幽州沿河北西路南下，兵鋒指向鎮州，另以耶律善補部趨河東路作牽制，企圖在宋軍三鎮分兵、彼此未及集中的空隙裡一舉撕開防線；其弱點正如趙廷進在高處所見——「東西互野，不見其尾」，人多而布陣不整，旗鼓號令難以壓住陣腳，韓匡嗣又中了宋軍詐降之計，誤判對方將來歸附。宋軍的部署是一套預先設計的鉗形殲滅：劉廷翰率先北進二百里，搶在徐河灘頭布陣並奪取河橋，把遼軍擋在河北岸；崔彥進潛師黑蘆堤北、緣長城口銜枚疾進，落到敵軍側後，切斷其往易州的退路；李漢瓊、崔翰兩部再由鎮州、定州方向靠攏會合，使徐河正面形成兩翼呼應之勢。決戰前的關鍵動作是變陣：太宗頒下的「平戎萬全陣圖」要求各陣相距百步，士卒心疑而氣餒，趙廷進主張合併為二陣、前後相輔，李繼隆以一己之責擔保違詔之罪，宋軍遂由散列改為互為照應的縱深配置。十月十八日先以爭橋之戰試探，奪橋後宋軍主力渡過徐河準備決戰；隨後宋軍以詐降拖住遼軍主帥，擂鼓全線突進，塵頭漲天，遼軍陣型被衝散，宋軍乘勝追擊至遂城，並以崔彥進的伏兵截斷退路。補給方面，宋軍依托關南、定州、鎮州沿線的城鎮與屯糧維持，遼軍則靠騎兵機動與就地取給支應，史料未載其輜重細數。
tacticsEn: The Liao adopted a plan of feinting on one front while driving straight in great depth on the other: the main host of one hundred thousand marched south from Youzhou along the Hebei west road with its point aimed at Zhenzhou, while a separate column under Yelü Shanbu was sent toward Hedong Circuit as a diversion, in the hope of tearing the line open during the interval in which the Song had split its strength among three towns and had not yet concentrated. The weakness of that formation was precisely what Zhao Tingjin saw from his vantage point: the enemy deployed east and west in open country with no tail in sight — many men, badly ordered, with flags and drums unable to hold the ranks together. Han Kuangsi then walked into the Song deception, believing the Song would come over to surrender. The Song deployment, by contrast, was a pincers annihilation designed in advance. Liu Tinghan pushed two hundred li north to seize the sandbank of the Xu River first and took the bridge, holding the Liao on the southern bank; Cui Yanjin moved by stealth through the north of Black Reed Bank along the Great Wall gap, soldiers holding their breath, to fall on the enemy's flank and rear and cut its road back toward Yi Prefecture; the columns of Li Hanqiong and Cui Han then closed up from Zhenzhou and Dingzhou to join, giving the Xu River front a mutually supporting shape. The key manoeuvre before the decisive action was the change of formation: the Perfect Array for Pacifying the Rong issued by Taizong required the lines to stand a hundred paces apart, which left the soldiers bewildered and disheartened. Zhao Tingjin proposed merging them into two lines supporting one another front and rear, Li Jilong took on himself the penalty for departing from the decree, and the Song army was thus converted from a scattered deployment into a deep formation in which each part covered the other. On the eighteenth of October the fight for the bridge served as a trial of strength; once the bridge was taken the main body crossed the Xu River to prepare for the decisive engagement. The Song then held the Liao commander with the false surrender, sounded the drums and launched a general assault that raised dust to the sky and broke the Liao order of battle, the Song pursuing as far as Suicheng while Cui Yanjin's ambushed column sealed the line of retreat. In the matter of supply, the Song drew on the walled towns and stored grain along the Guannan, Dingzhou and Zhenzhou line, while the Liao sustained themselves by cavalry mobility and foraging on the spot; the sources record no figure for their baggage train.
data: 時間：遼景宗於太平興國四年九月三日下詔南伐；九月三十日主力抵達滿城；十月十八日爭奪徐河橋；其後大戰與追擊至遂城，戰事約在十月十九日前後收束，歷時約一個半月。兵力：宋軍約八萬，據《宋史》卷二百七十一《趙廷進傳》，太宗命趙廷進與崔翰、李繼隆將兵八萬御敵，並賜陣圖分為八陣；遼軍約十萬，據曾瑞龍《經略幽燕：宋遼戰爭軍事災難的戰略分析》所引估計。空間：劉廷翰率眾北進二百里，先據徐河灘頭；崔彥進由黑蘆堤北緣長城口迂回；宋軍追擊至遂城，遼軍退向易州。戰果：斬首萬餘級，獲馬千餘匹，生擒遼將三人，俘老幼三萬戶，兵器軍帳甚眾；遼軍死亡約一萬、被俘約三萬。陣圖尺度：平戎萬全陣圖各陣相距百步。地理層面：自石敬瑭割讓幽雲十六州後，中原失去燕山屏障，易州、滿城、遂城、威虜軍一線地勢平坦而無天險；自979年至1004年的二十五年中，遼軍十次南侵有八次由這條中路防線突破，後來澶淵之盟時，遼軍騎兵正是繞過這條防線直趨黃河南岸。戰後處置：遼主以違眾深入、行伍不整、棄師鼠竄、偵候失機、捐棄旗鼓五罪責韓匡嗣，命即誅之，皇后力救得免，改以耶律休哥總南面戍兵。史料出處：《續資治通鑑長編》卷二十、《宋史》卷二百七十一與卷二百七十五、《遼史》卷八十三與卷九十七、《宋史紀事本末》；宋軍自身的損耗數字，各書皆不載。
dataEn: Timing: the Liao emperor Jingzong issued the order to invade on the third day of the ninth month of Taiping Xingguo 4; the main host reached Mancheng on the thirtieth of that month; the bridge over the Xu River was fought for on the eighteenth of the tenth month; the main battle and the pursuit to Suicheng followed, and the fighting closed around the nineteenth, giving a campaign of roughly a month and a half. Strength: the Song fielded about eighty thousand men — the History of Song, juan 271 in the biography of Zhao Tingjin, records that Taizong ordered Zhao Tingjin together with Cui Han and Li Jilong to take command of eighty thousand troops against the enemy and bestowed an array diagram dividing them into eight lines; the Liao fielded about one hundred thousand, an estimate cited by Tsang Sui-lung in his study of the Song-Liao war. Geography of the manoeuvre: Liu Tinghan led his men two hundred li north to occupy the sandbank of the Xu River first; Cui Yanjin came round by the north of Black Reed Bank along the Great Wall gap; the Song pursued to Suicheng while the Liao withdrew toward Yi Prefecture. Results: more than ten thousand of the enemy killed, more than a thousand horses captured, three Liao generals taken alive, some thirty thousand households of old and young captured, and a great quantity of weapons, banners and tents; on the Liao side, roughly ten thousand dead and thirty thousand prisoners. Scale of the formation: in the Perfect Array for Pacifying the Rong the lines stood a hundred paces apart. On the geographical plane, after Shi Jingtang ceded the Sixteen Prefectures the Central Plain lost the barrier of the Yan Mountains, and the Yi, Mancheng, Suicheng and Weilu line lay flat with no natural defence; of the ten Liao incursions into Song territory between 979 and 1004, eight came down this central route, and at the Chanyuan alliance the Liao cavalry would sweep past that very line to strike at the southern bank of the Yellow River. After the action the Liao ruler charged Han Kuangsi with five counts — advancing too deep against the general will, disorderly ranks, abandoning the army and fleeing like a rat, missing the opportunity in reconnaissance, and throwing away flags and drums — and ordered him executed; the empress interceded and he was reprieved, and command of the southern garrisons was given to Yelü Xiuge instead. Sources: Xu Zizhi Tongjian Changbian, juan 20; Song Shi, juan 271 and 275; Liao Shi, juan 83 and 97; Song Shi Jishi Benmo. No source records the Song losses in figures.
cause: 滿城之戰的直接起因是宋太宗永樂伐幽的一次失敗反噬。五月滅北漢之後，太宗不稍休，移師北上，企圖趁契丹新主初立、內部未固之際一舉收復幽雲十六州；六月大軍壓境幽州城下，卻在高梁河被耶律休哥、耶律斜軫等率騎兵大敗，宋軍崩潰，太宗中箭，乘驢車南逃，河北新得的土地隨即反覆。遼廷不願坐視燕京受圍之辱，景宗下詔南侵，名義上為報「圍燕之役」，實則要趁宋軍新敗、主力疲敝而河北防線空虛的窗口反守為攻。對宋廷而言，這是一場不能不接的戰：若遼騎再南下，關南、定州、鎮州一線失守，新併的北漢與中原邊防都將暴露在騎兵衝擊之下；宋太宗仍以一套由中樞頒下的標準陣圖來指揮前線，也說明他急於求勝而對契丹騎兵戰法缺乏理解。深層原因則是幽雲十六州割讓所留下的結構性矛盾：中原失去燕山屏障，河北平原暴露於北方騎兵，遼宋之間因此形成長達數十年、反覆拉鋸的邊境戰爭。
causeEn: The immediate occasion of the battle of Mancheng was the recoil from the failure of Taizong's campaign against Youzhou. After destroying the Northern Han in the fifth month the emperor did not rest but marched north again, hoping that while the new Khitan ruler had only just taken the throne and the state was still unsettled he might seize the Sixteen Prefectures of Yun-Yan in one stroke; in the sixth month the army pressed up to the walls of Youzhou, and at Gaolianghe it was beaten badly by Khitan cavalry under Yelü Xiuge and Yelü Shezhen, the Song host collapsing while the emperor was wounded and fled south on a donkey, and the territory newly taken in Hebei was thrown back into confusion. The Liao court would not sit and swallow the humiliation of the siege of Yanjing, and Jingzong ordered the southern invasion, nominally to avenge the siege, in truth to seize the window opened by the fresh Song defeat, by the exhaustion of the main army and by the hollow state of the Hebei defence line. For the Song court this was a battle that could not be declined: if the Liao horse came south again and the line of Guannan, Dingzhou and Zhenzhou fell, then the recently annexed Northern Han and the northern defence of the Central Plain alike would lie open to the cavalry charge. That the emperor still directed the front from the capital by a standard array issued from the centre shows that he was impatient for a decision and understood little of Khitan cavalry methods. The deeper cause lies in the structural contradiction left by the cession of the Sixteen Prefectures: with the Yan Mountains lost, the Hebei plain lay exposed to the northern horsemen, and so the Song-Liao frontier became a long, repeatedly contested war of attrition lasting several decades.
impact: 此役是宋遼戰爭的第一次戰局反轉。高梁河之敗後遼軍挾勝追擊、宋邊防一片悲觀的形勢，被徐河一戰扭轉：宋軍以正面迎敵加側後迂回的彈性防禦，抵銷了契丹騎兵在平原上的機動優勢，也證明只要指揮得當，遼軍的人多勢眾同樣會因部署鬆散而崩潰。香港中文大學的曾瑞龍把此役視為北宋初年彈性戰略防禦的典範，認為集中兵力打擊敵軍薄弱環節的做法，在其後的雁門之戰、羊山之戰中一再運用；王曉波則指出滿城與徐河的地形運用是取勝關鍵之一，滿城之戰與雁門之役共同遏制了高梁河之後遼軍的報復性反攻。對遼朝而言，這場敗仗的影響更為深遠：韓匡嗣被列五罪幾遭處死，兵權轉到耶律休哥手上，遼軍此後南下更倚重精銳騎兵與一線突破；二十五年後的澶淵之盟，遼軍正是以這種高速迂迴的騎兵戰法繞開宋軍步兵集團，兵鋒直抵黃河南岸。對宋軍而言，此役確立了河北中路防線的守禦樣式，前線將官在不敢違詔的顧慮中被迫品出「兵貴適變」四個字，也留下中樞命令與前線自主權如何取捨的長久命題。就兵器史而言，這是一個火器剛登上戰場、冷兵器仍獨當一面的年代：宋軍的火箭與火砲仍屬奇襲輔助手段，決定徐河勝負的仍是長矛、弓箭、橋梁與旗鼓。
impactEn: The battle was the first reversal of the course of the Song-Liao war. The gloom that had settled over the Song frontier after Gaolianghe, with the Liao pressing the attack in pursuit, was reversed in a single day at the Xu River: by meeting the enemy in front while wrapping around his rear, the Song elastic defence cancelled the mobility advantage of the Khitan horse on open ground, and it also demonstrated that a Liao host superior in numbers could be thrown into confusion by slack deployment if handled well. Tsang Sui-lung of the Chinese University of Hong Kong treats the engagement as a model of the elastic strategic defence built at the beginning of the Song, holding that the concentration of force against the weak point of the enemy was repeated in the later battles of Yanmen and Yangshan; Wang Xiaobo, for his part, points to the use made of the terrain of Mancheng and the Xu River as one of the keys to the victory, and notes that Mancheng together with Yanmen checked the Liao retaliatory offensives that followed Gaolianghe. For the Liao court the defeat was still more consequential: Han Kuangsi was charged with five counts and nearly executed, and the command passed to Yelü Xiuge, after which Liao invasions south relied more heavily on elite cavalry and penetration along a single line; twenty-five years later, at the Chanyuan alliance, Liao horse used exactly that fast flanking method to bypass the Song infantry masses and drive at the southern bank of the Yellow River. For the Song, the engagement established the defensive pattern of the central Hebei line, and the field officers, pressed as they were by the fear of disobeying the decree, were forced to learn the maxim that arms must adapt to circumstance; it also left standing the long question of how the orders of the centre and the freedom of the front are to be weighed against each other. In the history of weapons this was an age in which gunfire had only just appeared on the battlefield while cold weapons still bore the load alone: the Song fire-arrows and huo-pao remained instruments for surprise and support, and what decided the issue at the Xu River was still the spear, the bow, the bridge and the banners.
result: 宋軍勝。十月十八日之後，宋軍在徐河正面發動全線突進，遼軍大陣被衝散，韓匡嗣不聽耶律休哥勸阻而信宋軍詐降，此時已成追擊的最好時機；宋軍乘勝直追至遂城，斬首萬餘級，獲馬千餘匹，生擒遼軍將領三人，俘虜老幼三萬戶，收獲兵器與軍帳甚眾，韓匡嗣拋棄旗鼓，率殘部向易州方向遁走。遼軍另一路趨河東路的部隊同樣被宋軍擊退，兩路皆還，未能成事。事後遼主以五罪責韓匡嗣——違眾深入、行伍不整、棄師鼠竄、偵候失機、捐棄旗鼓——下令誅之，經皇后力救才免於一死，隨即命耶律休哥總領南面戍兵，遼軍的統帥與戰法自此轉向以精銳騎兵為骨幹。對宋軍來說，鎮州、定州、關南一線的防禦得以鞏固，河北中路的門戶穩住了；但此役未能收復任何燕雲土地，宋遼邊界仍大致維持在高梁河之戰後的狀態，兩國的長期對峙由此進入拉鋸與互有勝負的階段。關於宋軍自身的損耗，各種史籍皆無記載；遼軍被斬、被俘的數字雖見於《宋史》與《遼史》，雙方死傷的實際總量仍難以核實。
resultEn: The Song won. After the eighteenth of October the Song army launched a general assault on the Xu River front, the great Liao deployment broke apart, and Han Kuangsi, who had ignored Yelü Xiuge's counsel and believed the Song offer of surrender, was now in the best possible position to be chased; the Song pursued as far as Suicheng, killing more than ten thousand, taking more than a thousand horses, capturing three Liao commanders alive, taking some thirty thousand households of old and young, and gathering up a great quantity of weapons, banners and tents, while Han Kuangsi threw away his flags and drums and fled with the remnants toward Yi Prefecture. The other Liao column that had moved toward Hedong Circuit was likewise driven back, and neither column achieved its object. Afterwards the Liao ruler charged Han Kuangsi with the five counts — advancing too deep against the general will, disorderly ranks, abandoning the army and fleeing like a rat, missing the opportunity in reconnaissance, and throwing away flags and drums — and ordered him put to death; he was reprieved only through the intercession of the empress, and Yelü Xiuge was then given overall command of the southern garrisons, so that the Liao command and the Liao way of war turned from that date towards an elite cavalry core. For the Song the defence of the Zhenzhou, Dingzhou and Guannan line was consolidated and the door of the central Hebei front held firm; but no territory in Yun-Yan was recovered, the Song-Liao border remained broadly where it had stood after Gaolianghe, and the long confrontation between the two states entered a period of grinding alternation in which each side won and lost. As for the Song losses, no historical work records them; and although the figures for the Liao dead and captured appear in the History of Song and the History of Liao, the true total of casualties on both sides cannot be verified.
